draft.text: You came in to check your overall health and ask if you need to take any extra steps.
You have mild leg puffiness and feel dizzy when standing up quickly.
Your blood pressure drops by 15/10 mmHg when you stand up.
The dizziness may be due to your blood pressure dropping when you stand up, called orthostatic hypotension.
You will keep checking your blood pressure and report any changes.
You should drink more fluids and keep taking your medicines as prescribed.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been feeling some puffiness in your legs and have been experiencing dizziness when standing up quickly.
We found that your blood pressure drops by 15/10 mmHg when you stand up, which is called orthostatic hypotension.
Your blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg when lying down and 105/70 mmHg when standing up.
The dizziness when standing up is likely related to your beta-blocker medication.
The puffiness in your legs may be related to your medications, but the exact cause is not clear.
You should continue to monitor your blood pressure and report any changes to your healthcare provider.
You may want to increase your fluid intake to help manage the dizziness.
Continue taking your medications as prescribed and report any changes in your symptoms or blood pressure.
